sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
The window is not a smooth compounder: FY2019 operating margin collapsed 11.9pp to 8.1% and net income fell 60.0% [F23][D109][F33][D98].
That trough was an $8.3 billion before-tax Shave Care impairment charge, $6.8 billion of it goodwill, driven by currency devaluations and decelerating grooming category growth [X109][X112][P62].
FY2020 then rebounded 14.0pp on operating margin as the base-period charge fell away and gross margin rose on manufacturing savings, lower commodity costs and higher pricing [D160][P65][P71].
The US was the growth engine for most of the window, contributing +3.4pp of FY2021 revenue growth and +2.7pp in FY2023 [D521][D527].
In FY2026 the mix flipped: Non-US contributed +3.1pp of the 3.3% growth while the US added just +0.1pp [D511][D457][D536].
FY2026 net sales rose on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Beauty was the largest segment contributor at +1.3pp, growing 7.1% to $16.0 billion, while Fabric & Home Care added +0.8pp on 2.4% growth [D603][D602][S45][D543][D542].
Operating income grew 4.1% a year against 3.3% revenue growth, but FY2026 operating income fell 3.4% while revenue rose 3.3% [F202][F201][D458][D457].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sits 0.6pp above the 22.1% window median but 1.6pp below the FY2025 high of 24.3% [F30][D648][D647][D470].
The FY2026 decline came from cost of revenue adding 1.0pp of margin drag and SG&A 0.6pp, as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix and marketing spending rose [D483][D485][P25][P5].
The FY2025 gain of 2.2pp was the mirror image, with SG&A easing 0.8pp and other lines adding 1.7pp [D419][D433][D434].
Below the line, other non-operating income of $1.1 billion lifted pre-tax income 1.0% despite the operating decline, holding net margin at 18.4% [X108][P22][F50].
Operating margin ranks in the 80th percentile of five staples peers against a 14.3% median [D668][D669].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income in FY2026, while free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x, below the 1.02x free-cash-flow window median [F80][F40][D444][F100][D445][D660].
The 9.8% operating cash flow increase came from net earnings plus non-cash items, with payables generating $919 million offset by inventory consuming $641 million for safety stock [D462][P3].
Free cash flow of $15.1 billion was a 17.4% margin, above the 17.2% median, after capex rose 16.9% to $4.4 billion, or 5.1% of revenue [F100][D441][D654][D464][F90][D440].
Capex now runs at 1.40x depreciation and amortization, the highest ratio in the window [D446].
Net debt of $24.2 billion is 27.8% of revenue, a larger net cash deficit than the -1.0% peer median, ranking only the 33rd percentile of six peers [D450][D451][D677][D676].
Cash of $9.9 billion against $34.1 billion total debt leaves a 0.68x current ratio, below the 0.72x window median [F140][D449][F180][D663].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [X134][X144][D453][D476].
Return on average equity of 30.1% trails the 44.4% peer median, ranking 33rd percentile of six [D456][D681][D680].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x in every year of the window and fell to 0.68x in FY2026, a persistent negative working-capital position [F180][F171][R1].
For a staples business with steady cash generation this reflects deliberate low liquidity rather than distress, but it leaves little buffer [R1].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 at 116.6% and again in FY2026 at 100.7%, funded partly by debt [D402][D453][R2].
Two consecutive years of over-distribution is the more material flag because it caps the pace of deleveraging [R2].
Operating margin: a FY2027 print below the 22.1% window median would confirm the FY2026 cost pressure, while a return above the 24.3% FY2025 high would reverse it [D648][D647].
Free cash flow margin: holding above the 17.2% median depends on capex staying near 5.1% of revenue rather than climbing further [D654][D440].
Buybacks plus dividends against free cash flow: a third year above 100.7% would extend the FY2026 pattern, while a drop below the 86.6% FY2024 level would signal deleveraging [D453][D350].
